toolsPanel_restrictedDescription: Chrome blocks extensions from running on chrome:// pages, other extensions' pages, the Chrome Web Store, and the built-in PDF viewer. No extension can reach into this tab, so it will never have page tools, whatever the page itself supports. Chat and server tools still work here.
toolsPanel_webmcpOffDescription: document.modelContext doesn't exist here. WebMCP is off by default in Chrome, and no page can use it until you launch with --enable-features=WebMCP, turn on chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing, or open a site carrying an origin-trial token. This is not a page that registered no tools; there was nothing here to ask.
toolsPanel_noPageToolsDescription1: That's expected: most sites don't speak WebMCP yet. It's a proposed web standard that lets a page publish named actions and page-state readers (“add a note”, “read the cart total”) on document.modelContext, so a model can call them directly instead of clicking through the interface. Same idea as MCP, but for what a website itself chooses to offer, rather than a separate server.
toolsPanel_noPageToolsDescription2: A site opts in by calling registerTool() in its own page script. If this page did, its tools would appear here the moment it registered them. Nothing for you to refresh or configure.
toolsPanel_noServerToolsDescription: Add a server in the options page's MCP servers section and enable it. A server that's slow, unreachable, or not yet permitted simply contributes no tools here; it never blocks anything.

mcpServersSection_description: An MCP server offers tools that have nothing to do with the current page: a ticket tracker, a search index, an internal service. Its tools join the same list the page's own tools appear in, namespaced by server so nothing collides. A server tool call is judged by its own, stricter approval policy, not the page's. See “MCP server tool approval” above.

settingsSection_approvalDescription: When a call to one of the page's own WebMCP tools runs straight away, and when it waits for you to approve it first.
settingsSection_defaultPolicyDescription: Tools the page marks read-only run automatically, shown as a collapsed card in the chat. Every other tool call waits for your approval, including the ones with no hint at all.
settingsSection_alwaysConfirmPolicyDescr: Every tool call waits for your approval, even the ones the page marks read-only. Slower, but nothing runs without you seeing it first.
settingsSection_autoRunAllPolicyDescript: Every tool call runs immediately, with no approval step at all, including calls that submit forms, delete data, send messages, or otherwise change a site you're signed in to. The model acts on your behalf and you never get to review a call first. Choose this only if you trust both the model you're chatting with and every site you open the side panel on.
settingsSection_safetyAnnotationsNotice: Safety hints like readOnlyHint come from the page itself and the extension can't verify them: a hostile page can label a genuinely destructive tool read-only to slip it past this setting. Treat this as guidance for the ordinary case, not a security boundary. The real boundary is which sites you open the side panel on and grant the extension permission to reach. Every call, approved or automatic, is recorded in the call log, so nothing happens invisibly.
settingsSection_mcpApprovalDescription: When a call to one of your MCP servers' tools runs straight away, and when it waits for your approval. This is a separate setting from “Tool approval” above; changing one never changes the other.
settingsSection_mcpAlwaysConfirmDescript: Every server tool call waits for your approval, whatever the server claims about being read-only. You can't see what a remote call did the way you can watch a page, so this is the strictest of the three options here, and deliberately stricter than the page default above.
settingsSection_mcpSafetyNotice: You can't watch a remote server the way you can watch the page in front of you, and one call can reach an account, a repository, or a ticket queue rather than a single tab. That's why this setting starts at “Always confirm” instead of mirroring the page policy, and why the two stay fully independent. Add or remove servers in the MCP servers section below.
settingsSection_mcpTrustReadOnlyDescript: Tools an MCP server marks read-only run automatically, shown as a collapsed card in the chat, the same as the page policy's default. Choose this only for servers you trust to report that hint honestly: it's a claim the server makes about itself, and the extension can't check it.
settingsSection_mcpAutoRunAllDescription: Every server tool call runs immediately, with no approval step at all, including calls that change or delete data on a service signed in as you, out of sight of whatever you're looking at. Choose this only if you trust every server you've added below.
